body:
## Why political literacy is important

KNOWLEDGE IS POWER.

Political literacy is crucial to understanding the political world of today. Political literacy allows the average citizen to know where each candidate stands and what policies they stand for. Political impartiality is also a crucial aspect of political literacy as impartiality (as hard as it is) teaches people to abandon their personal biases in favor of being able to understand and communicate with people who share political ideals that are different from yours.

BE A GOOD ACTOR IN TODAY’S DEMOCRACY

To vote for the president, mayor, senator, representative, or governor you want, you need to understand their policies and what they have planned if they assume this position of power. Dictators and authoritarian regimes rely on collective ignorance to gain and keep power.

## The left: Communism

Founded by Karl Marx and Fredrich Engels

Calls for the abolishment of free markets and the private ownership of industries is favor of a command economy

Economy and economic decisions are determined by the government

Nationalized (government controlled) industries

Mobilizes the working class, especially the peasantry.

## The left: Socialism

Also founded by Marx and Engels

Supposed to be a transition stage to communism

Think of it like communism + capitalism = socialism

still, socialism opposes capitalism

calls for workers to own the industries they are apart of instead of CEO’s and shareholders

Democratic socialists support democratically run governments and a decentralized socialist economy

Famous figure: Fidel Castro

## The left and center: Liberalism

Founded by philosopher John Locke.

Supports the notion that the government should grant an individual certain rights and liberties.

Liberals believe the government must protect its citizens from danger (attacks, disease, poverty, etc).

Liberal governments promote democracy.

citizens vote for their leaders and representatives.

## The left and center: Bipartisanship

Advocates for the collaboration and cooperation of the two parties

Focuses on Moderation and Compromise: Policies created through bipartisan efforts often reflect moderate and balanced viewpoints

An example is the Civil Rights Act of 1964

Popular figures are Maggie Hassan and George H.W. Bush

## The center and right: Tripartisanship

NOT a third party, dismisses the need for third parties.

Advocates for a group of independent politicians leveraging reforms like open primaries.

These independent politicians can be acting mediators on high-profile issues like immigration and national debt.

## The center and right: The Republican Party

Founded in 1792 by Thomas Jefferson.

Jefferson favored a decentralized government with limited power (AKA states’ rights).

Supports Laissez-faire capitalism and low taxes.

Oppose government intervention in the economy (affirmative action, gov’t funding of social programs.

Support strong national defense and increased military spending

Popular figures: Mitt Romney and Liz Cheney.

## The right: The conservative movement

Very religious

Roots in Evangelicism and Christian Fundamentalism.

Conservatives look to traditional political and cultural institutions to curb humans’ base and destructive instincts.

Many modern-day republicans are conservatives

Popular figures: Donald Trump and Mike Pence

## The right: Fascism

Founded in 1919 by Benito Mussolini with the Italian National Fascist party

Fascist leaders utilize extreme nationalism, propaganda, and economic instability to gain supporters

Led by powerful dictator

Gov suppresses political opposition and criticism

No free press

Strong emphasis on military power

Hardship is essential for a fascist government to survive and flourish
